aria: Animated recap of the Suns' 117 to 105 road win over the Nuggets: Devin Booker's 17-foot jumper in the last two minutes that pushed Phoenix's lead back to 10, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Booker's 20 points and 8 assists, the top scorers, how the Suns won, and the next game at Sacramento.
notes: Box score from the Suns' 117–105 win over the Denver Nuggets at Ball Arena in Denver on Nov 16, 2026, from the Covers.com box score, with game details from the Associated Press (via ABC News), Field Level Media, Bright Side of the Sun (via Yahoo Sports), the Denver Post, the Denver Gazette, Denver Stiffs, SI.com and Sport News Africa. All 117 Phoenix points and all 105 Denver points are accounted for in the box score, and the quarter scores add up to both totals: Denver led 24–20 after one, Phoenix led 56–53 at the half and 90–82 after three. Team totals (field goals 43 of 88 to 40 of 83, threes 16 of 36 to 9 of 30, free throws 15 of 25 to 16 of 19, rebounds 51–35, offensive rebounds 18–9) are from the Covers box score; the Denver Post gives the same threes and AP the same rebounds. Second-chance points (22–11) and bench points (42–19) are from AP and the Denver Gazette; Phoenix's 42 bench points also match the box score. Points in the paint (44–50) are from Covers. The game had 14 ties and 10 lead changes before Phoenix pulled away in the third quarter (AP). The Suns' biggest lead, 19, came at 107–88 in the fourth quarter (AP; Field Level Media; Covers). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Monday's games.

Denver hit three 3-pointers early in the third quarter to lead 62–59 (Field Level Media; Denver Post) before Phoenix took over; Nikola Jokić had 28 points, 15 rebounds and 7 assists with 7 turnovers (Covers; SI.com). Jamal Murray scored 28, with 18 in the fourth quarter (Field Level Media; Denver Gazette). Seven Suns scored in double figures (Covers; Bright Side of the Sun). Denver got within 8 with 43 seconds left (AP). It was Phoenix's first road win of the season, on the second night of a back-to-back after a 131–123 loss to the Lakers on Sunday (AP). The Suns play at Sacramento on Wednesday, Nov 18 (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Devin Booker's 17-foot jumper late in the shot clock that pushed the lead back to 10 at 113–103, right after Murray's three free throws with 1:46 left made it 111–103 (Field Level Media: "Booker hit a jumper late in the shot clock to push the lead to 10"; Bright Side of the Sun: "Devin Booker responded by burying a big 17-footer to push the lead back to 10"). No source gives the exact time of the shot, so the game clock is not shown. It is drawn as the template's plain pull-up. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Phoenix Suns or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Booker's listed 6-foot-5 and 206 pounds (Basketball-Reference), with his arms scaled to the 6-foot-8¼ wingspan measured at the 2015 NBA Draft Combine (Tankathon), in the Suns' road colors with No. 15, the number he switched to for 2026-27 (ABC15; Arizona Sports). His look is from the site's look sheet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
